report.source_text: Since the plasma hyperosmolality associated with urine hypoosmolality persisted, central diabetes insipidus was suspected and a water deprivation test was carried out. Based on copeptin levels during thirsting (copeptin t0–4.3 pmol/l; copeptin t7–4.2 pmol/l) and response to desmopressin, we diagnosed central diabetes insipidus (Table 1). The polyuria of up to 12 L / d was normalized during the following days by application of desmopressin.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 49-year-old male presented with severe frontal to occipital headaches, photophobia, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Imaging with CT and MRI revealed a haemorrhagic sellar mass diagnostic of subacute pituitary apoplexy. Laboratory tests showed persistent plasma hyperosmolality with urine hypoosmolality. A water deprivation test with copeptin measurement and desmopressin treatment confirmed and managed central diabetes insipidus characterized by polyuria up to 12 L/day which normalized after desmopressin. Pituitary insufficiencies of multiple axes were also documented after admission.
